rationale: Newsletter operators and content curators are a well-defined B2B/prosumer buyer with a clear budget: they already pay for Feedly Pro ($8/mo), Inoreader ($10/mo), and similar data-pipeline tools, confirming willingness to pay at the target price point. The pain is real and recurring — YouTube RSS outages are a chronic, documented problem that breaks automated workflows these users depend on daily. The service (a reliable YouTube channel monitoring proxy with email/webhook alerts) is fully buildable with Claude + a simple web scraper/YouTube API fallback + a form + Stripe, and delivery is entirely automated once live — operational autonomy is high with no per-customer manual work required.
solution_plan: WHAT: A paid YouTube channel monitoring service — subscribers enter channel URLs, and the service checks for new videos on a schedule and delivers alerts via email or webhook, bypassing unreliable RSS. BUILD: The factory builds a Claude-orchestrated backend that polls YouTube channels (via the Data API v3 or HTML scraping as fallback when RSS fails), a simple sign-up form/landing page, and a Stripe subscription link ($9–19/mo) — no coding by the operator; the factory handles the cron logic and alert emails. SELL: Outreach targets newsletter operators (Substack, Ghost communities), podcast producers (r/podcasting), and developer automation forums (n8n, Zapier communities) — the factory drafts cold outreach messages and posts them only after the operator approves each batch. MAINTAIN: New video alerts are generated and emailed by Claude + code automatically; Stripe manages billing and cancellations; Claude handles support tickets (FAQs about adding channels, alert delays); the operator's only recurring task is reviewing and approving outreach sends roughly once a week. SCALE PATH: If traction emerges, add Slack/Discord webhook delivery and multi-channel bundles — all automatable within the existing factory tooling.
notes: All build gates pass: operational_autonomy=8 (≥7), buildability_with_ai=8 (≥6), buyer_clarity=7 (≥6), willingness_to_pay=7 (≥5). Note: YouTube API quota limits and ToS on scraping should be reviewed before launch — use the official Data API v3 to stay within ToS. Defensibility is modest (4); first-mover advantage in reliability/alerting UX is the main moat.
